THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT Heard Sri.Sharath S. Gowda learned counsel for the appellant.

Though Sri.V.K.Narayanaswamy,
learned counsel is on record representing the respondent, he has failed to make his appearance and submit his contentions.
2. Challenge in this appeal is the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal at Bengaluru in MVC No.3667/2013 dated 07.02.2015.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal at Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This is a claimant's appeal.

3. Making his submission with regard to the merits of the matter, learned counsel for the appellant states as against the claim of Rs.20,00,000/-, the Tribunal has awarded a meager sum of Rs.1,76,759/- as compensation and therefore, seeking enhancement, the present appeal is preferred.
Learned counsel also states that the appellant sustained one grievous injury and one simple injury.
He further submits that the appellant took extensive treatment by getting admitted in the hospital.

Learned counsel submits that without considering NC: 2023:KHC:45808 the oral and documentary evidence produced, the Tribunal awarded compensation which is disproportionate to the loss sustained.
4.

A perusal of the record goes to show that the Tribunal which dealt with the matter, subjecting the evidence of PWs-1 and 2 and Exs.P1 to P23 to scrutiny came to a conclusion that the appellant sustained injuries in a road traffic accident and that the disability in respect of whole body is 15%.

The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.35,000/- under the head 'pain and agony', Rs.66,769/- under the head 'medical expenses', Rs.81,000/- towards disability, Rs.9,000/- towards 'attendant charges',
Rs.10,000/- towards 'food and nourishment ' and in total Rs.2,01,769/-.
5.

Making a submission that the income of the minor child cannot be assessed and therefore,
calculation of loss in certainty, cannot be arrived at, learned counsel relied upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of MALLIKARJUN v. DIVISIONAL MANAGER, NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND ANOTHER - NC: 2023:KHC:45808 (2014)14 SCC 396, wherein their Lordship's at paragraph 12 of the judgment held as follows:-
"12.

entities.text: MALLIKARJUN v. DIVISIONAL MANAGER, NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED AND ANOTHER - NC: 2023:KHC:45808 (2014)14 SCC 396
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various High Courts,
Venkataramanachari.

2

we are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc. should be, if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to the whole body, Rs.3 lakhs; up to 60%, Rs.4 lakhs; up to 90%, Rs.5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be Rs.6 lakhs.
For permanent disability up to 10%, it should be Rs.1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take a different yardstick."

6. Thus, in the light of the aforementioned decision and as observed by the Tribunal and borne by record, the disability is 15% in respect of the whole body, Rs.3,00,000/- ought to have been granted under the head 'pain and suffering' already undergone and to be suffered in future, medical and physical hardship, inconvenience, discomfort and loss of amenities in life.

Thus, the compensation which the appellant is entitled to under different heads is as under:-
NC: 2023:KHC:45808 Sl.
Description Amount No Rs.

1 Compensation for pain and  suffering which the  appellant already  underwent and to suffer in  3,00,000  future, inconvenience,
 discomfort and loss of  amenities in life on account  of permanent disability  2 Medical expenses 66,769  3 Attendant charges 9,000  4 Food and nourishment 10,000
Total Compensation Rs.3,85,769  7.
Thus, the appeal is allowed in part.
The compensation awarded by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bangalore, is enhanced from Rs.1,76,759/- to Rs.3,85,769/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry the same interest as awarded by the Tribunal from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
The award of the Tribunal in all other aspects holds good.

Sd/-
JUDGE VMB Venkataramanachari.
